probes.input:
;; Clojure's mod is floored division; rem is truncated. They agree on
;; positive operands and disagree on a negative dividend, so a probe using
;; only positive operands cannot tell the two apart. v1.0.0's P02_arithmetic
;; is exactly that blind case (expected_output ""). Expected values are
;; Clojure's, confirmed against `ys -p -e`: (-7 %% 3) = 2, (-7 % 3) = -1.
;; See compound-packs/yamlscript-semantics/modulo-is-not-remainder.md.
(def a (mod -7 3))
(def b (rem -7 3))
(say a)
(say b)

expected_output.description: mod vs rem on a negative dividend: mod floors (2), rem truncates (-1)

probes.input:
;; clj-to-ys.py _binding_coll: a literal vector cannot sit in an `each`
;; binding position, so a contiguous ascending run of integer literals becomes
;; a YS range and anything else is hoisted into a temp binding. Both branches
;; are here; no probe covered this emitter branch before v1.2.0.
(doseq [x [1 2 3]]
  (say x))

(doseq [y [1 5 3]]
  (say y))

expected_output.description: _binding_coll: contiguous literals become an inclusive YS range, non-contiguous hoist to a temp
